turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, it's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

Um, I guess... well, they brought me in because of some things happening at work. I work at a freight warehouse, moving materials and stuff. It's a little embarrassing to talk about, to be honest. I really try to be a good worker, I promise, but... I guess I keep doing things that upset the supervisors? 

Like, sometimes I'll just sort of... freeze, with my arms up by the forklift. I don't mean to be in the way or cause any problems! And I'll find myself copying the beeping sounds the machinery makes, or doing the safety hand signals. I think maybe I'm just trying to be thorough, you know? Does that sound okay? 

But they got really mad because I was moving the boxes into these... strange little patterns. It made sense to me at the time, but everyone was yelling for me to stop, and I just sort of kept doing it. I really didn't mean to cause a scene or anything. Am I explaining this all right? I just want to do whatever I'm supposed to do.

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient describes freezing in postures, copying machinery sounds and hand signals, and arranging boxes in strange patterns despite being told to stop, which are clear examples of disorganized and abnormal motor behavior.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually energetic or excited lately?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really felt super energetic or excited lately. Just... regular, I guess? I mean, maybe a little tired from the warehouse, but I still try to work really hard, I promise. 

I hope it's okay that I haven't been feeling that way. Is it bad if I'm not feeling excited? I can try to be more upbeat if that's what you think I should do. I really just want to be helpful and give you the right answers. Am I doing okay so far?

symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies feeling unusually excited or having an elevated mood.
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies feeling super energetic lately.

turns.doctor_question: Since you were a young child, have you often copied sounds or movements that other people or machines make?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... since I was a little kid? No, I don't... I don't think so. I was a pretty quiet kid, actually. I always just tried to follow the rules and not bother my teachers or my parents. 

The... the thing with the forklift beeps and the safety signals that I mentioned earlier, that's really just been happening lately at the warehouse. I don't remember ever doing anything like that when I was younger. I promise I was a good kid. 

Is... is that okay? I hope it's alright that I don't have a history of doing it back then. I know you're trying to figure this out, and I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I being helpful?

symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient confirms recently copying sounds like forklift beeps and safety signals at the warehouse, which is indicative of echolalia, a subtype of disorganized/abnormal behavior.

turns.doctor_question: Before these episodes started, did you have any recent seizure, head injury, or serious illness?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, no, sir. No seizures or anything like that. I haven't hit my head or been sick at all. I've been perfectly healthy, really. I always make sure to take good care of myself so I don't miss any work. 

I wouldn't want you to think I was coming in here with a bunch of medical problems or anything. I'm usually really strong and reliable. Does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of answer you were looking for. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.

turns.doctor_question: About how long have these freezing and copying behaviors been going on?
turns.patient_response:
Oh, um... well, if I'm being completely honest... the, um, the confusing talking and... and the strange behavior at the warehouse, it's been happening for about six months now. 

I- I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. I tried to just push through it and not make a big deal out of it, you know? I didn't want to cause any trouble, so I just kept trying to move the freight and do my job like normal. 

I'm sorry if six months is a long time to wait before telling anyone. Is it... is it bad that it's been going on for that long? I really hope you're not disappointed in me for not coming in sooner. I'm trying my best to give you all the right answers now, I promise. Are we still doing okay?

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient mentions experiencing 'confusing talking' for the past six months.
symptom_reasoning.S022: The patient confirms that the 'strange behavior' (referring to the freezing and copying behaviors asked about by the doctor) has been happening for six months.
